# Results — Study 487 (Elder's Triple Screen)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **align
three timeframes (weekly trend up, daily oscillator oversold, breakout entry) and you get a
high-odds long** — encoded as a mechanical rule. Screen 1 is the slope of a *weekly*
MACD-histogram (read on completed weeks, shifted one day — no look-ahead); Screen 2 is a daily
Force-Index proxy dipping below zero within the last 5 bars (the pullback); Screen 3 is a close
above the prior bar's high (the breakout trigger). A long fires when all three align, entered at
the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **2369** mechanical triple-screen longs pooled across the 5 tapes |
| Timing / costs | weekly trend shifted **+1 day**; oscillator/breakout read on close of *t*; enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument trend study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — triple-screen vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch triple-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = triple − random.

| horizon | n | triple | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (triple−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 2368 | +10.9 bps | 55% | +2.10 | +24.9 bps | **−14.0 bps** | +8.9 bps | −1.92 | 0.054 |
| 10-day | 2363 | +31.9 bps | 60% | +3.77 | +29.7 bps | **+2.3 bps** | +29.9 bps | +0.22 | 0.823 |
| 20-day | 2352 | +74.9 bps | 61% | +5.21 | +68.5 bps | **+6.4 bps** | +72.9 bps | +0.44 | 0.657 |
| 60-day | 2344 | +220.1 bps | 67% | +5.97 | +257.3 bps | **−37.1 bps** | +218.1 bps | −1.54 | 0.123 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+5.21** at 20 days,
**+5.97** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the triple-screen entry is
*worse* at 5 and 60 days (Δ = −14.0 / −37.1 bps) and only trivially better at 10/20 days
(+2.3 / +6.4 bps). The triple-minus-random difference **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar**
(max Welch *t* = +0.44 at 20 days, *p* = 0.657; the only near-2 reading is −1.92 at 5 days — i.e.
the filter is, if anything, *worse* than a dart at the short horizon). The three screens do not
forecast.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the filter does not beat random in any coherent way

| ticker | entries | triple | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (triple−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 477 | +69.0 bps | +2.75 | +69.7 bps | **−0.7 bps** |
| QQQ | 464 | +113.1 bps | +3.60 | +93.8 bps | **+19.3 bps** |
| IWM | 473 | +64.4 bps | +1.84 | +15.1 bps | **+49.3 bps** |
| DIA | 438 | +43.9 bps | +1.44 | +57.4 bps | **−13.5 bps** |
| GLD | 517 | +81.8 bps | +2.26 | +103.1 bps | **−21.3 bps** |

The delta is **negative in 3 of 5** names; the two positives (QQQ +19, IWM +49) are small and
unaccompanied by a significant pooled signal. No coherent cross-sectional edge — the hallmark of
relabelled drift.

## Screen-scramble placebo — shift the trend filter, nothing changes

The decisive "does the timeframe alignment matter?" test: keep each screen's **marginal**
frequency but circularly **shift** the weekly-trend boolean relative to price, destroying the
multi-timeframe alignment. If the three screens genuinely combine into an edge, the scramble
would collapse the result.

| test | observed triple 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY screen-scramble | +69.0 bps | **0.649** | 500 |

**65% of scrambled-alignment runs match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.649). The specific
weekly-to-daily alignment carries no information — a misaligned trend filter does just as well.
"The multi-timeframe filter adds edge" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real bounce

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* triple-screen bounce (knob `edge`), the same rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a
dead detector.

| planted edge | n | triple | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no bounce) | 296 | −2.9 bps | 50% | −0.07 |
| **0.50** (real planted bounce) | 275 | +543.3 bps | 77% | **+8.29** |

With no planted bounce the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted bounce
lights up at *t* = +8.29 with a 77% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The triple-screen long does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (triple − random = −14.0 / +2.3 / +6.4 / −37.1 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the triple-vs-random
  Welch *t* never clears 2, max +0.44 at 20 days, and is actually −1.92 at 5 days). The
  impressive one-sample *t*'s (20-day +5.21, 60-day +5.97) are pure beta — the upward drift of
  long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more
  fully by holding the index; the three-screen rule trades less and pays costs on each trigger,
  dominating nothing. No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Does the multi-timeframe filter add edge"? — BUSTED.** The screen-scramble placebo leaves
  the result intact (*p* = 0.649): a misaligned trend filter does as well as the real one, so the
  weekly-to-daily alignment carries no forecasting information. Triple Screen is a sensible
  trade-*management* discipline, not a forecasting edge.
